prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1368; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. For the record, can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision in Katy, Texas?
A: Yes, I was driving my own car that day.
Q: Walk me through what happened, starting from when you first noticed the other vehicle.
A: I was heading down the two-lane road, maybe going around twenty-five miles an hour because of the traffic. The other car drifted into my lane and I tried to swerve, but we still hit nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, honestly, more of a jolt.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. I just got pushed back into the seat and my wrist hit the steering wheel and the door frame.
Q: Did you hit your head or lose consciousness at any point?
A: No, I stayed awake the whole time. My head didn't hit anything.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle on your own?
A: I did. My wrist was throbbing right away, so I held it against my chest and waited for the police.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same afternoon. They took X-rays and said it was a fracture in my wrist. I've got a splint now and I'm following up with an orthopedic doctor.
Q: Did you have any prior injuries to that wrist or arm?
A: No, nothing before this.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the collision?
A: Just that I'm right-handed, so it's been hard getting things done at home. That's about it.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
